result.title: Two For The Price Of One: Curvature-Aware Pruning Preserves Influence Functions Too
result.summary: Post-training pruning enables efficient deployment, but conventional methods do not explicitly preserve internal-gradient alignment between sparse and dense models. We study novel connections between downstream performance of compressed models and the ability to retain gradient information via influence-function preservation. Central to this connection is a curvature-aware objective that accounts for both layer activations and backpropagated gradients. Despite its promise, this objective remains underexplored in pruning due to a lack of efficient solvers. We introduce $\texttt{CACTUS}$, a novel ADMM-based optimizer supporting both pruning and sparse-plus-low-rank decompositions of pre-trained weights. Compared to LLM-Surgeon which targets the same objective, $\texttt{CACTUS}$ can achieve over an order-of-magnitude speedup. At $50\%$ pruning of Qwen3-4B, $\texttt{CACTUS}$ reduces the C4 perplexity gap to the dense model by $45\%$, improves compressed-to-dense per-sample gradient cosine similarity on WikiText-2 from $0.670$ to $0.755$, and runs over $28\times$ faster than LLM-Surgeon on substantially weaker hardware. By preserving influence functions, $\texttt{CACTUS}$ supports effective data selection. On Llama-3.2-3B, fine-tuning a fresh dense model on the $5\%$ of data selected by $\texttt{CACTUS}$ achieves $49.44\%$ accuracy on BIG-Bench Hard, compared with $47.22\%$ using ALPS and $49.54\%$ using dense-model selection. Finally, integrating $\texttt{CACTUS}$ with LoGRA, a recent gradient-projection strategy, on Qwen3-4B with MLP layers pruned to 2:4 sparsity and a rank-64 correction retains a $0.711$ cosine alignment with dense LoGRA-projected C4 gradients.

AI.brief_summary: 论文研究后训练剪枝中如何保持压缩模型与稠密模型的影响函数（梯度）对齐，提出基于 ADMM 的优化器 CACTUS，同时支持剪枝与稀疏加低秩分解，显著加速剪枝并改善困惑度与逐样本梯度余弦相似度，还可用于数据选择。
AI.relevance_reason: 其以「压缩—稠密」逐样本梯度余弦相似度量化内部信息保留、并用影响函数做训练数据选择的做法，可能为 LVR 中 latent 状态是否保留任务必要信息、以及轨迹训练的数据与贡献分配提供可核查的度量线索，但论文本身未涉及视觉或多模态推理，迁移属推测。
